To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cell intrinsic transcriptional changes in Alzheimer’s disease are detectable through deconvolution methods, that these changes are robustly replicating across brain regions and cohorts, and that they provide novel insights into disease mechanisms.
we developed an in-house algorithm and compared it to two existing algorithms to detect cell-intrinsic differentially expressed genes across three independent AD and control cohorts.
we developed and applied a bioinformatics pipeline to identify consensus cell intrinsic differentially expression genes in individual cell type in AD and control brains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of computational tools to identify cell-intrinsic gene expression differences in bulk-tissues and their applications in Alzheimer’s disease research.

the identification of transcriptional changes in specific brain cell types in Alzheimer's disease, which is a major challenge in the study of this disease, as the brain contains many different cell types.

the identification and characterization of cell-intrinsic transcription changes that are associated with Alzheimer’s disease (a neurodegenerative disorder that is the leading cause of dementia in the elderly).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cell-type-specific alterations are present in Alzheimer’s disease and that these alterations are not captured by bulk-tissue RNA-seq.
the cell-intrinsic transcription of individual cell types can be reliably inferred from bulk RNA sequencing data.
the cell-type specific gene expression alterations identified by our pipeline are promising and should be further investigated in independent datasets and by other computational approaches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed and applied an innovative bioinformatic approach to identify transcriptional changes in individual cell types in Alzheimer's disease brains, which is a critical step to understand cell-intrinsic molecular changes in neurodegenerative diseases.
we have identified cell intrinsic gene expression changes in Alzheimer’s disease and that these changes are robustly replicating across multiple brain regions.
we have developed a computational pipeline for detecting cell-intrinsic differentially expressed genes (CI-DEG) in bulk RNA-seq datasets of brain tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of bulk-tissue RNAseq to identify cell-intrinsic gene expression alterations is feasible and may provide novel insights into disease mechanisms.
bulk RNAseq data can be used to infer cell-intrinsic transcription changes in individual cell types.
cell-type specific transcriptional changes in AD are robustly replicating across brain regions, and are largely missed in bulk RNAseq studies.
